source: K original phase qubits, IID uniform full labels A over Z_(2^t)^n, one fixed unknown secret, and independent original Z faults with probability1/(2n)
frame: For F_f={x:A*x=f}, |F_(f,e)>=|F_f|^(-1/2)*sum_x (-1)^(e.x)|x>, for a FIXED error set E independent of A and the realized error
exact_moments: For fixed nonzero binary d independent of A, E_A sum_f B_f(d)^2=2^K*(1-1/q^n)
For M fixed error patterns, E_A sum_f (d_f/2^K)*||Gram_f-I||_F^2 <=4*M*(M-1)*(q^n-1)/2^K
conditional_transform: On Gram-error-squared<1 fibers use polar orthogonalization and a public unitary mapping the frame basis to the SAME error-pattern computational basis across all frequencies. Use identity on bad fibers; do not reject them. This is an exponential reference, not a supplied polynomial circuit.
information_only_bound: At K=2*n*t, E includes every original error of weight<=2t. A suitable arbitrary controlled frame unitary has source-average parity failure <=0.5*sqrt((q^n-1)/2^K)+sqrt(20*M*(M-1)*(q^n-1)/2^K)+(11/16)^t, capped1; uniform for each fixed secret.
proof_obligations: Keep error-pattern library independent of labels, secret and actual faults; no hidden-error oracle
Use actual Born fiber weights, not a uniform average of normalized rare fibers
Retain coherent full-frequency branches and align error bases/phases across paired frequencies
Derive and cost a uniform finite-gate transform without exponential fiber/error enumeration, dense SVD, free QRAM, or arbitrary input erasure
Charge all bad frames, noise tails, original sample calls, approximation, ancillas and natural-source preparation
positive_countercontrols: Known orthogonal error modes admit actual coherent correction using a public unitary that never receives the realized fault
Nonorthogonal near-identity frames have actual approximate polar transport with a verified state-distance bound
Binary-rowspace error aliases shift the secret by q/2 times a binary vector, preserving the first-secret parity for t>=2; Gram-near-identity is sufficient, NOT necessary
falsifiers: A complete native label census violates the fixed-difference signed moment or the Born-normalized frame bound
An actual controlled-unitary circuit violates the polar/state-distance estimate
A native error tail is treated as absent or a source mean becomes a per-matrix/all-error guarantee
An efficient-decoder claim substitutes approximate orthogonality, known dense matrices or a private realized error for a uniform circuit
